content.value_statement: Adding a new FlashInfer kernel requires coordinated C++, Python, JIT, test, and benchmark changes. This skill gives a structured workflow that an AI coding assistant can follow safely.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to define a templated CUDA kernel in FlashInfer include files.
Shows how to create a C++ launcher and TVM-FFI binding for tensor inputs.
Guides Python JIT generator and public API setup for a new operation.
Covers CUDA architecture targeting with CompilationContext examples.
Outlines unit tests, AOT registration, exports, and benchmark additions.
limitations: Focused on FlashInfer repository conventions and CUDA kernel workflows.
Uses an element-wise scale kernel as the main example.
Does not replace code review for memory safety or performance correctness.
Requires CUDA, PyTorch, and FlashInfer development knowledge.

use_cases.title: Add a Simple GPU Operation
use_cases.description: Implement a small element-wise FlashInfer kernel with API, tests, and benchmarks.

use_cases.title: Extend FlashInfer Python APIs
use_cases.description: Connect a new CUDA implementation to TVM-FFI and expose it through a Python function.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kernel Validation Work
use_cases.description: Create tests, architecture checks, AOT registration, and benchmark coverage for a new kernel.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Kernel Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a new FlashInfer element-wise CUDA kernel. List the files to create or modify before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Implement the JIT Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add the JIT generator and TVM-FFI binding for my new FlashInfer kernel.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tests and Exports
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add pytest coverage, Python exports, and AOT registration for the new kernel.

prompt_templates.title: Review Kernel Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my FlashInfer kernel integration for missing architecture checks, API gaps, tests, and benchmarks.

output_examples.input: Add a scale kernel to FlashInfer.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step implementation plan covering CUDA source, launcher, binding, JIT generator, Python API, tests, exports, and benchmark work.

output_examples.input: Check whether my kernel needs architecture guards.
output_examples.output: A review of supported compute capabilities, recommended CompilationContext settings, and test skip conditions for unsupported GPUs.

output_examples.input: Prepare validation for a new kernel.
output_examples.output: A testing and benchmarking checklist with dtype coverage, reference comparisons, error cases, AOT registration, and timing measurements.

best_practices: Keep CUDA headers framework-agnostic and place TVM-FFI logic in csrc files.
Add dtype dispatch, architecture checks, and clear error handling before exposing the API.
Ship tests and benchmarks with every new kernel to protect correctness and performance.
anti_patterns: Do not put Torch or TVM-FFI dependencies into generic CUDA include headers.
Do not skip validation unless the caller controls all inputs and accepts the risk.
Do not add a kernel without tests, exports, AOT registration, and performance coverage.

faq.question: What type of skill is this?
faq.answer: It is a coding guide for adding CUDA kernels to the FlashInfer project.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready kernels automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and examples that still require engineering review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code assisted coding workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes pytest coverage across dtypes, sizes, correctness checks, and error cases.

faq.question: Does it cover performance measurement?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes benchmark guidance using FlashInfer testing utilities.

faq.question: What should users verify manually?
faq.answer: Users should verify memory safety, numerical accuracy, supported GPU architectures, and repository-specific integration details.
